hints: Complete the square for $x^2 - 4x$ as $(x-2)^2 - 4$ and simplify.
walkthrough:
Factor out $-3$ from the quadratic and linear terms and complete the square:
$$-3x^2 + 12x + 2 = -3(x^2 - 4x) + 2 = -3\left((x - 2)^2 - 4\right) + 2$$

hints: Find the $x$-coordinate of the vertex of the parabola.
walkthrough:
Identify the axis of symmetry and vertex $x$-coordinate of the parabola from part (a):
$$x = 2$$

State the greatest possible value of $k$ such that the restricted function on $x \le k$ is one-to-one:
$$k = 2$$

Evaluate $f(-1)$ to find the maximum value of $f(x)$ on the interval $x \le -1$:
$$f(-1) = -3(-1 - 2)^2 + 14 = -3(9) + 14 = -27 + 14 = -13$$

State the range of $f$ since the function is strictly increasing up to $x = -1$:
$$f(x) \le -13 \quad (\text{or } y \le -13)$$

hints: Take the negative square root since $x \le 2$.
walkthrough:
Set $y = -3(x - 2)^2 + 14$ and rearrange to isolate $(x - 2)^2$:
$$3(x - 2)^2 = 14 - y \implies (x - 2)^2 = \frac{14 - y}{3}$$

Take the negative square root since the domain is $x \le 2$ (so $x - 2 \le 0$):
$$x - 2 = -\sqrt{\frac{14 - y}{3}} \implies x = 2 - \sqrt{\frac{14 - y}{3}}$$

Write the inverse function in terms of $x$:
$$f^{-1}(x) = 2 - \sqrt{\frac{14 - x}{3}}$$

Apply the translation by vector $\begin{pmatrix} -3 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$ by substituting $x \to x + 3$ and adding $1$ to the completed square form:
$$g(x) = -3((x + 3) - 2)^2 + 14 + 1 = -3(x + 1)^2 + 15$$

Simplify into standard quadratic form $px^2 + qx + r$:
$$g(x) = -3x^2 - 6x + 12$$
